ai.description: This large frog reaches 17 cm. It is olive-green or brownish with dark spots and a prominent pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a pointed snout and a vibrant yellow throat during breeding.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hoplobatrachus tigerinus* is best identified by the prominent, longitudinal skin folds (dorsolateral ridges) on its back and its distinctly pointed, triangular snout.
ai.habitat: The Indian bullfrog inhabits freshwater wetlands, marshes, and paddy fields across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: During the monsoon, the Indian Bullfrog becomes highly active and vocal, with males inflating bright yellow vocal sacs to attract mates in flooded fields.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Indian Bullfrog is oviparous, breeding during the monsoon (June–August). Females lay large clutches of 3,000–6,000 eggs in shallow, temporary water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian bullfrog is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, inhabiting diverse elevations from sea level up to 2,000 meters across most Indian states.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Bullfrog emits a series of loud, low-pitched, resonant "gawk-gawk" calls, typically heard from flooded fields and marshes during the monsoon breeding season.
